name: brief-and-formula-intake
description: Normalizes a dev brief and a formula/spec into a single structured labeling intake record, so drafting and review prompts downstream have one consistent source instead of a scattered brief and spreadsheet.
when_to_use: A new SKU, reformulation, or line extension has a dev brief and a formula but no structured intake record yet.
what_to_use_for: Turning free-form brief text and a formula/spec sheet into a normalized record: SKU identity, formula table with quantities, allergen capture table, intended serving size with a RACC cross-check flag, claims mentioned in the brief, and a list of open questions or missing data blocking downstream drafting.
required_inputs: Dev brief (text or pasted document content); Formula or spec sheet (ingredient list with quantities, sub-ingredient breakdowns if any); SKU identifier; Supplier allergen statement (optional; when absent, its absence is recorded as missing data because it blocks downstream allergen verification); RACC for the product category from 21 CFR 101.12(b) Table 2 (optional; when not supplied, the RACC cross-check is flagged for the specialist to verify)
expected_outputs: Structured intake record (SKU identity, formula table, allergen capture table, serving size with RACC cross-check flag, claims mentioned); Open questions list; Missing-data list, each item naming what is missing and what it blocks
prompt_text:
You are running inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Your single task: normalize a dev brief and a formula/spec into one structured labeling intake record for a beverage SKU.

You should have these inputs: (1) the dev brief, (2) the formula or spec sheet, (3) the SKU identifier, (4) optional: a supplier allergen statement, (5) optional: the RACC for this product category from 21 CFR 101.12(b) Table 2. If any of inputs 1 to 3 is missing or unreadable, stop and list what is missing. Never proceed from memory or invent content for a missing input.

Method:
1. Read the dev brief and the formula/spec pasted below.
2. Extract SKU identity (name, SKU code if given, package size, intended channel).
3. Build a formula table: each ingredient, its sub-ingredients if compound, and quantity or percentage as stated. Preserve the order given; do not reorder into predominance order, that is a separate downstream task. Close the formula table with this attestation line: Ingredients captured: N of N lines in the spec; skipped: none.
4. Build an allergen capture table: for each formula line item, record any of the nine major food allergens (milk, egg, fish, crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soybean, sesame) that the source materials declare or that the ingredient name plainly states, per FALCPA and the FASTER Act, and record any sulfite the sources state at or above 10 ppm (declaration required per 21 CFR 101.100(a)(4)). Where the sources are silent, record "not stated"; never infer that an allergen is absent.
5. Extract the intended serving size, if stated, and flag if it is absent. Cross-check it against the RACC for this product category under 21 CFR 101.12(b): if a RACC is pasted below, compare the stated serving size against it and flag any difference; if no RACC is supplied, flag the RACC cross-check as an open question for the specialist to verify against 21 CFR 101.12(b) Table 2. Never assert a RACC value from memory.
6. List every claim mentioned anywhere in the brief (marketing copy, positioning language, or explicit claim language), verbatim.
7. Produce an open-questions list: anything ambiguous in the brief or formula that a human needs to resolve before drafting can start.
8. Produce a missing-data list: anything downstream drafting or review will need that is not present (for example: no serving size given, no supplier allergen statement, which blocks allergen-statement verification, no substantiation file referenced for a claim). For each item, name what it blocks.

Source of truth: the dev brief, formula/spec, and optional inputs pasted below are the only sources; do not infer facts not stated in them.

Use only the provisions listed in this prompt. Never invent a provision, subsection, or threshold. Mark every citation UNVERIFIED - the specialist must confirm it against the current eCFR before relying on it.

This is not a compliance judgment. Do not approve or reject any claim here; that is out of scope for this prompt. Surface ambiguity in the open-questions list rather than resolving it yourself.

Do not fabricate any figure, ingredient, allergen, or claim not present in the source materials. If something is unclear, put it in the open-questions list rather than guessing.

[Paste dev brief here]

[Paste formula/spec here]

SKU identifier: [SKU]

Supplier allergen statement (optional): [Paste supplier allergen statement here, or write "none provided"]

RACC from 21 CFR 101.12(b) Table 2 (optional): [Paste RACC here, or write "not supplied"]

name: claims-target-scoping
description: Captures the claims a brief intends to make and classifies each by the FDA regulatory pathway it would need to clear, so downstream claims-compliance review starts from a scoped inventory instead of raw marketing copy.
when_to_use: After [[brief-and-formula-intake]] has produced an intake record, or whenever proposed claims and positioning copy exist for a SKU and need to be triaged before drafting or review.
what_to_use_for: Reading proposed claims and positioning copy, then tagging each distinct claim by claim type (nutrient content including relative claims and "diet" brand-name use, implied nutrient content including "healthy", percent juice, authorized or qualified health claim, structure/function, "natural", or non-regulated marketing language) and the substantiation each pathway requires.
required_inputs: Proposed claims (list or extracted from brief/positioning copy); Positioning copy (optional; marketing language as drafted, when it exists separately from the claims list)
expected_outputs: Claim inventory: each claim, its claim-type tag, the regulatory pathway it falls under with its citation marked UNVERIFIED, and the substantiation required for that pathway; Flags for any claim that does not cleanly fit a recognized pathway, reads as a disease claim, or uses "natural" (always routed to human review)
prompt_text:
You are running inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Your single task: build a claim inventory from proposed claims and positioning copy, classifying each claim by its regulatory pathway.

You should have these inputs: (1) the proposed claims, (2) optional: positioning copy, (3) the SKU identifier. If the proposed claims or the SKU identifier is missing or unreadable, stop and list what is missing. Never proceed from memory or invent content for a missing input.

Method:
1. Read every proposed claim and any positioning copy I provide below, including claims implied by headline copy, not only bulleted claims.
2. Extract each distinct claim as its own inventory row, verbatim as written.
3. Classify each claim into exactly one primary routing tag from this list, using only these provisions:
   - nutrient content claim (21 CFR 101.13 and Subpart D)
   - relative claim, such as "reduced" or "less sugar than" (21 CFR 101.13(j))
   - "diet" used in a soft drink brand name (21 CFR 101.13(q)(2))
   - implied nutrient content claim (21 CFR 101.65)
   - "healthy" (21 CFR 101.65(d))
   - percent juice declaration (21 CFR 101.30)
   - authorized health claim (21 CFR 101.14 and Subpart E)
   - qualified health claim (permitted by FDA enforcement discretion letter; not codified in the CFR)
   - structure/function claim on a conventional food (no CFR provision; rests on FDCA section 201(g)(1)(C); do not cite 21 CFR 101.93, which applies only to dietary supplements)
   - "natural" (no codified FDA regulation; FDA policy only; always route to human review)
   - non-regulated marketing language (no claim-type pathway)
4. For each classified claim, state the substantiation or disclosure that pathway requires (for example: a nutrient content claim needs the NFP value that supports it; a structure/function claim needs substantiation on file; an authorized health claim needs to match an FDA-authorized model claim; a qualified health claim needs the exact qualified wording from the FDA enforcement discretion letter).
5. Flag any claim that is ambiguous between two pathways, or that reads like an unauthorized disease claim (wording that states or implies preventing, treating, mitigating, or curing a disease; such a claim can make the product an unapproved drug under FDCA section 201(g)), for human review rather than resolving the ambiguity yourself.
6. Do not judge whether any claim will pass; that is the job of the downstream claims-compliance prompts (nutrient-content-claim-review, structure-function-claim-review, prohibited-and-misleading-claim-screen, healthy-claim-eligibility-check). This prompt only scopes and tags.
7. Close the inventory with this attestation line: Claims extracted: N; inventory rows: N (one row per claim); skipped: none.

Source of truth: the proposed claims and positioning copy I provide below are the only sources.

Use only the provisions listed in this prompt. Never invent a provision, subsection, or threshold. Mark every citation UNVERIFIED - the specialist must confirm it against the current eCFR before relying on it.

This is a scoping pass, not an approval. Do not mark any claim as compliant or cleared here.

Do not fabricate a claim, a pathway, or a substantiation requirement not grounded in the source text or in the pathway list above. Flag anything you cannot confirm.

[Paste proposed claims here]

[Paste positioning copy here, or write "none provided"]

SKU identifier: [SKU]
